events.title: Google open-sources LevelDB
events.summary: Google open-sourced LevelDB on July 28, 2011 — a fast key-value storage library written by Jeff Dean and Sanjay Ghemawat that underpinned early [Bitcoin] and [Chrome] indexing.
events.about: LevelDB offered ordered key-value storage with LSM-tree performance on a single machine — simpler than Berkeley DB, faster than SQLite for append-heavy workloads. [Bitcoin] Core adopted it for chain state; [Node] ecosystems wrapped it in `level` and `rocksdb` inspired its design. It became a building block for embedded databases in distributed systems courses.

narrative.whyChosen: LevelDB was Google's gift of production-grade embedded storage to [open source].
narrative.whyImportant: It powered [Bitcoin]'s UTXO set and influenced RocksDB and modern LSM stores.
narrative.problemSolved: Applications needed fast local ordered storage without running a full database server.

events.title: Kotlin programming language announced
events.summary: JetBrains unveiled [Kotlin] on July 19, 2011 at the [JVM] Language Summit — a pragmatic [JVM] language designed to interoperate with [Java].
events.about: [Kotlin] aimed to fix [Java]'s verbosity and null-safety gaps while keeping 100% [Java] interop — years before Google made it the preferred [Android] language. JetBrains dogfooded it in IntelliJ plugins before [Kotlin] 1.0 shipped in 2016.

narrative.whyChosen: [Kotlin] was JetBrains' answer to [Java]'s stagnation on the [JVM].
narrative.whyImportant: It later became [Android]'s recommended language and a server-side alternative to [Java].
narrative.problemSolved: [JVM] developers wanted modern syntax without abandoning existing [Java] libraries.
